commits.subject: fix(picks): grade suspended-game picks from pre-suspension PA, not the boxscore
commits.body:
The production scorer read the cumulative final boxscore hit total, which includes the
resumed portion of a suspended game -- so a resumed-portion hit could falsely continue a
streak. Grade suspended-and-resumed games from pre-suspension plays only (startTime <
resumeDateTime): a hit before suspension is a hit, a pre-suspension PA with no hit is a
miss, and a batter present only in the resumed portion is a void. _check_hit_in_game
stays suspension-aware for the bool callers (shadow_eval, skip_policy_shadow); check_hit
gains an opt-in return_status, used by the streak path, so void reaches the streak.
Normal games are unchanged (the whole branch is gated on resumeDateTime).

commits.subject: fix(experiment): exclude resumed-portion PA from BTS scoring + calibration
commits.body:
The live-forward resolver and the (batter_id, date) day-hit lookups in calibrate,
realized_calibration, and canonicalize_realized_picks all took max(is_hit) over a
suspended game's full PA -- so a resumed-portion hit could be credited to an
original-gameday pick (a pre-suspension out flipped to a hit; a calibration label
inflated). Route these through read_pa_for_bts_scoring / filter_out_resumed_portion so
only pre-suspension PA count. A batter with only resumed PA becomes a missing outcome,
which the final-game void routing resolves as void_no_pa (pre-suspension PA with no hit
is a miss). The skill-pool prior_pa/hit_rate lookup is intentionally left unfiltered --
resumed PA are legitimate events for ability estimates. Also names void_suspended_resume
in the resolved-manifest prose (the one gap from the prior deploy).

commits.subject: fix: address review round 1 — broaden suspended-game scoring coverage
commits.body:
Codex review (with repo access) found four real issues, all fixed:
- BLOCKER: an all-resumed suspended game (zero pre-suspension PA) stalled the resolver
  pending, because outcome_game_keys was derived from the resumed-excluded outcomes.
  Derive it from UNFILTERED PA dates so the final-game routing void_no_pa's the
  original-day candidate instead of re-triggering the resolution alert.
- scheduler._check_hits_midgame read cumulative boxscore hits directly; route it through
  the suspension-aware picks._check_hit_in_game so a live resumed-portion hit cannot
  advance the streak mid-game.
- health/slate_auc built realized BTS labels from raw max(is_hit); read via
  read_pa_for_bts_scoring so the realized AUC monitor excludes the resumed portion.
- build marked a missing-startTime PA as pre-suspension while the production scorer
  treats it as resumed; align build to the conservative (resumed) direction.

Feature computation (experiment/features.py) and the skill-pool prior keep resumed PA by
design (real baseball events); research/audit scripts are left unfiltered (negligible
impact, not production scoring).

commits.subject: fix(shadow-eval): preserve suspended-game void in the cached-feed backfill path
commits.body:
The final holistic review found an 8th consumer: `bts shadow-backfill-results`, on its
cached-raw-feed path, graded picks with the bool _check_hit_in_game -- which collapses a
suspended-game "void" (resumed-only PA) to False -> "miss". So --apply could write a
reviewed shadow result as a miss instead of a void. Extract check_hit's internal feed
grader as a module-level picks.grade_pick_in_feed ("hit"/"miss"/"void"/None) and use it on
the cached path (_hit_to_slot_result already handles "void"). The live-API path
(resolve_pick_slot_result) was already correct; scheduler mid-game keeps the bool
_check_hit_in_game since it only needs hit/no-hit.
